ec140_utility_max_application (constrained utility maximisation via Lagrangian) and ec109_utility_maximisation (utility maximisation subject to budget constraint) describe the same underlying mechanism/model but exist as separate disconnected nodes in different modules with no merge or cross-link, causing redundant teaching.
ec140_cost_min_application (constrained cost minimisation via Lagrangian) and ec109_cost_minimisation describe the same underlying optimisation problem but are disconnected across modules.

GDP limitations node discusses ignoring distribution of income, which is a distinct taught concept (income inequality measurement) elsewhere in EC108; also this is a rule-19/rule-7 style bundling of multiple independent critiques (non-market activity, distribution, externalities, leisure) that could be split, but at minimum the distribution point should link to the inequality subtopic.

This node bundles four independently markable costs of inflation (menu costs, shoe-leather costs, redistributive effects, uncertainty/investment effects) into one node, violating rule 7/19 - a real mark scheme credits these as separate distinguishable points.

new_nodes.label: Menu costs and shoe-leather costs of inflation
new_nodes.objective: Understand menu costs and shoe-leather costs as resource costs of inflation.
essentialPoints: Menu costs: firms incur costs of repricing goods
Shoe-leather costs: costs of holding less cash and more frequent bank visits

new_nodes.label: Redistributive and uncertainty costs of inflation
new_nodes.objective: Understand redistributive effects between creditors/debtors and uncertainty costs of inflation.
essentialPoints: Redistributive effects between creditors and debtors under unexpected inflation
Uncertainty discourages investment and long-term planning

issues.explanation: There is a malformed/duplicate stray edge object in the nodes array (an edge-shaped object with 'from'/'to' fields mixed into the nodes list) which is invalid and creates a dangling/duplicate reference to ec124_spearman outside the edges array.

Rule 16: this node bundles the concept of utility maximisation with reading/deriving the tangency condition on the indifference-curve/budget-line diagram; construction of indifference curves and budget lines are separate nodes already but the application/diagram-reading step for finding tangency itself is compressed into this one node without a distinct application node separating 'concept of optimum' from 'diagram-based tangency solving', though this is a minor compression given existing structure.

Set for fiscal policy currently only has one advantages node bundling 3 points (direct AD boost, targeting, multiplier) versus disadvantages having 4 points - the advantages side is thin relative to a real mark scheme which would credit distinct points such as 'no reliance on private sector response' or 'can be targeted regionally/structurally distinct from monetary policy', and 'addresses market failure/public goods directly'.

new_nodes.label: Fiscal policy can be precisely targeted at sectors, regions or groups
new_nodes.objective: Understand that fiscal policy can target specific sectors, regions or income groups unlike broad monetary policy.
essentialPoints: Government spending or tax changes can be directed at specific industries, regions or households in need
This precision is not available to economy-wide interest rate changes
